 Early voting for December 12 election begins November 28 in Caddo Parish
 November 18, 2026 November 18, 2026 / JSLLC 
 Early voting for the Saturday, December 12, 2026 election in Caddo Parish will run from Saturday, November 28 through Saturday, December 5 , giving registered voters an opportunity to cast their ballots ahead of Election Day.
 Key Dates & Voting Information 
 Early Voting Period: Saturday, November 28 – Saturday, December 5, 2026
 Election Day: Saturday, December 12, 2026
 Registration & Absentee Deadlines: Voters can verify exact online registration cutoffs, absentee mail ballot request and return deadlines, and daily polling hours through the Louisiana Secretary of State’s GeauxVote Voter Portal or by contacting the Caddo Parish Registrar of Voters.
 Caddo Parish Sample Ballot (December 12, 2026) Note: Actual ballot items vary by municipality and district. Contests and propositions appearing on the Caddo Parish December 12 ballot include: 
 Caddo Parish School Board (for eligible district voters) :
 District 2: Marvkevea Campbell (Democrat) vs. Kenneth J. Coutee (Democrat)
 District 5: Courtney N. Harris (Democrat) vs. Karla McCulloch (Democrat)
 District 6: Dana Fergins-Hawthorne (Democrat) vs. Cleveland Mouton III (Democrat)
 District 12: Larry Wilson (Democrat) vs. Sheila “Crosby” Wimberly (Democrat)
 City of Shreveport Municipal Contests (for eligible municipal voters) :
 Mayor: Tom Arceneaux (Republican) vs. Stormy Gage Watts (Democrat)
 City Council, District F: Billy Roy Anderson Jr. (Democrat) vs. Lester Smith (Democrat)
 City Court Judge: Kharmen Davis-Taylor (Democrat) vs. Sheva Sims (Democrat)
 Local Tax Propositions (for eligible district voters) :
 Shreveport-Bossier Convention and Tourist Bureau: Renewal of the 1.5% hotel-motel occupancy tax for 12 years (through 2039)
 Voters in eligible fire and municipal districts can confirm any additional local propositions on their personalized sample ballot. 
 Where to Vote Early in Caddo Parish Early voting locations can differ from Election Day precincts. Voters in Caddo Parish can confirm their designated early voting site, daily operating hours, and local Registrar of Voters contact details through the Louisiana Secretary of State’s GeauxVote Voter Portal, the Caddo Parish Registrar of Voters, or the Caddo Parish Clerk of Court.
 What to Bring Voters casting a ballot in person are typically asked to bring a valid form of photo identification—such as a Louisiana driver’s license, a Louisiana special ID card, a LA Wallet digital driver’s license, or another generally recognized picture ID containing their name and signature. Voters without an accepted photo ID can confirm alternative verification options with election officials at the polls.
 Voters can review their personalized sample ballot, check their registration status, and confirm their Election Day polling place through the Louisiana Secretary of State’s GeauxVote Voter Portal or by contacting the Caddo Parish Registrar of Voters.
